items.prose: Colliers thatched sixty cords of dense white oak billets beneath a dual layer of moist grass turf and damp loam. Restricting draft air through adjustable bottom pegs throttled direct combustion into slow, oxygen-starved coaling across five days.

Long thermocouple iron spears tracked the downward advance of the 485°C exothermic pyrolysis wave. As radiant heat reached the lower periphery, operators sealed upper vent pegs and opened low draft vents to guide uniform carbonization.

The exhaust plume evolved from thick, pungent white steam to heavy acrid yellow wood gas, before transitioning into a thin, shimmering blue haze. The blue smoke confirmed that volatile tars had driven off, leaving only pure incandescent fixed carbon.

An internal bridging cavity collapsed the sod mantle, admitting a sudden inrush of oxygen that triggered an open flame blowout. Colliers furiously shoveled twenty wheelbarrows of wet silt across the breach within three minutes to extinguish the flare.

Cooling the completed coaling mound with fine atomized water mist through sealed draft holes quenched residual embers without thermal shock cracking. The hickory lump charcoal remained in large, dense fist-sized chunks with ringing metallic resonance.

Pyrolyzing twelve tons of air-dried white ash billets yielded 3.05 tons of high-grade metallurgical charcoal. The lustrous black fracture faces exhibited zero uncharred brown brands and an electrical resistivity below 10 ohms/cm.

Unloading dry charcoal lumps inside the stagnant air of Sub-Level 3 generated suspended clouds of 40-micron charcoal fines. Grounding all sorting screens and misting unloading chutes with 2% clay water eliminated electrostatic deflagration hazards.

Replacing earthen mounds with segmented 10-gauge steel cylindrical kilns fitted with perimeter sand-trough seals cut turn-around cycle time from seven days to forty-eight hours. Black locust yields reached an unprecedented 29.5% with near-zero ash loss.
